headline: A quick-hitting coastal storm brings rain Sunday afternoon into Monday morning — 1–2 inches is possible, though the latest models favor the heaviest rain east of New York City — and another, potentially stronger coastal storm is possible Wednesday night into Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: High pressure keeps New York City and the region dry and quiet through Saturday and Saturday night. Winds stay light, turning from the east-southeast at around 5 mph on Saturday. No watches, warnings or advisories are in effect.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: A low-pressure system moving up the coast could bring a few showers Sunday morning into early afternoon, with more widespread rain Sunday evening and overnight before it ends early Monday. Rainfall of 1–2 inches is possible across much of the area, with up to 3 inches locally if a persistent band of heavy rain sets up, and a few thunderstorms are possible; the overnight models shifted the storm slightly east, so the heaviest rain now looks more likely over eastern areas, and some models show a sharp cutoff with very little rain for NYC and points west. There is a low-end risk of flooding of city streets, poorly drained areas and small streams, and east winds of 10–15 mph Sunday night could gust to 25–30 mph along the coast (a small chance of 40–45 mph gusts in a small area farther east). Monday brings clearing with northwest gusts around 15–25 mph, and Tuesday looks quiet.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Wednesday daytime looks quiet, with a chance of light rain arriving Wednesday night. Models agree a potentially large coastal storm may develop Wednesday night into Thanksgiving Day, with the potential for stronger winds and more coastal flooding than Sunday's storm. The weather pattern is complex, so small changes could make big differences in the storm's strength, track and timing — it's one to keep watching.

coast: Coastal flooding from Sunday night's storm looks minimal because Monday morning's high tide comes after the storm has passed, though a few Long Island south shore back-bay spots could approach or just reach minor flood levels with the full moon approaching on Tuesday. The Wednesday night–Thanksgiving storm could bring more significant coastal flooding, depending on its track and strength. On the water, small-craft-advisory conditions are likely on most of the ocean waters, eastern Long Island Sound and the eastern Long Island bays Sunday night into Monday (more sheltered waters stay just below that level for now), with a chance of gales on the ocean and eastern Sound and bays Sunday night; rough ocean conditions likely last into at least Tuesday as waves are slow to settle, and gales are possible on all waters Wednesday night.
watch_for: Where Sunday night's heaviest rain sets up: it currently favors eastern areas, but the storm could still shift the heavy rain back west toward NYC.
The storm's exact track, which decides how windy the coast gets Sunday night.
The Wednesday night–Thanksgiving coastal storm and its potential for strong winds and coastal flooding.
confidence: Forecasters are fairly confident in rain Sunday night into Monday but uncertain about where the heaviest rain and strongest winds fall, and the Thanksgiving storm's track and impacts remain highly uncertain.
